TEXT.English: Piye ruled Napatan Kush in the eighth century BCE and campaigned into Egypt. His royal inscriptions emphasize Amun and the legitimacy of kingship. This package draws on Napatan religious institutions rather than the much later ironworking identity often associated with Meroe. The cult chapel is a repeatable gameplay institution, not a claim that an identical royal monument stood in every settlement.

TEXT.English: Stefan Dusan ruled a fourteenth-century Serbian empire and promulgated his law code in 1349. The Vlastela represents medieval noble cavalry, while the court and mining-based economy abstract legal administration and developed mining settlements. These are not later Hajduk, Chetnik or modern cavalry formations. The Priest's Espionage represents literate institutions in the game's specialist system, not a historical claim about a spy religion.

TEXT.English: Matthias Corvinus ruled Hungary from 1458 to 1490. His paid forces included early handgun troops, while his court supported Renaissance learning. The college abstracts scholarly patronage rather than placing copies of the royal library in every city. The Black Army's professionalism came with real financial costs. The unit uses the game's Gunpowder tier, not later mounted Cuirassier equipment.

TEXT.English: Pedro II reigned in Brazil from 1831 to 1889 and cultivated scientific and scholarly interests. The Voluntarios da Patria represents forces raised during the 1860s war, but recruitment was not uniformly voluntary: coercion and slavery must not be erased from that history. The Lyceum represents educational institutions rather than a claim that the emperor built an identical royal college in every city.

The Lyceum represents educational institutions rather than a claim that the emperor built an identical royal college in every city.
